title: UVW profile, version 1
$comment: The graph envelope over the candidate: a world is spaces plus connections. Each space carries ONE primitive topology; the candidate document body (basis/bounds/layers) becomes the body of one heightfield space, so a candidate document is exactly a profile document with a single space and no connections. Connections are RESERVED at zero entries in this version: SC2 and Warzone need none, and minting connection schemas before a publisher exists is the lie the world-interchange registry note forbids. The connection amendment (portal/seam with affine mappings, scale, wrap, dynamic anchors) is designed in ../../design/DESIGN_UVW_TOPOLOGIES.md and lifts maxItems when the first consumer lands. Modkit migrates its UVW writer from the candidate to this profile in GA wave 4; until then both schemas are current, candidate marked superseded-by.

spaces.$comment: At least one. Space ids must be unique — uniqueness across objects is a composition check, not expressible here. Ordering is canonical by id; the graph has no privileged first space, a viewer picks an entry space by convention (lowest id) unless a package says otherwise.

connections.$comment: RESERVED: zero entries in profile v1. The amendment defines portal (point anchors, pass rules, affine mapping incl. scale) and seam (boundary gluing incl. self-seams for wrap) and lifts this cap.

space.$comment: topology names the whole catalog so the day a publisher lands the name is already taken by the right thing (the candidate's own reservation pattern); only heightfield is admitted by this version — the oneOf below is the single gate to widen.

basis.$comment: Verbatim the candidate's ProjectionBasis: canonical frame pinned, only the unit story varies; source-unit forbids inventing a metre factor (SPEC_UV_COORDINATES section 2).

kind.$comment: heightfield is defined; the rest are reserved names, unchanged from the candidate.

samples.$comment: row-major: `rows` arrays of `columns` numbers. Sample counts, not cell counts — the usual off-by-one.
